taxable: A margin loan is available in this account, so the sleeve can sit on top of a full stock position. Funds that carry the exposure inside are available here too.

Taxes are not modelled. Stock index funds defer most of their gain until sold. The sleeve is taxed harder: Treasury interest is ordinary income (free of state tax), funds holding gold bullion are taxed as collectibles, and managed-futures funds pay out most of their return as taxable distributions.
The replay rebalances every month. In this account a sale can realise a gain.
traditional: A retirement account cannot take a margin loan. Exposure above 100% of capital can only come from funds that carry it inside.
Nothing is taxed until withdrawal, and withdrawals are taxed as ordinary income whatever was held. No holding is tax-favoured over another, and rebalancing costs no tax.
roth: A retirement account cannot take a margin loan. Exposure above 100% of capital can only come from funds that carry it inside.
Qualified withdrawals are untaxed. No holding is tax-favoured over another, and rebalancing costs no tax.

financing.stacked: funds that carry the exposure inside
